subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Jacobs <tom.jacobs@acme.com>
Cc: Sara Lee <sara.lee@acme.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist and next steps

Hi Tom / Sara —

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Per our demo and the discovery notes, I wanted to capture the recommended next steps and a shortlist of models that strike the right balance for Acme's use case (customer support summarization + lightweight QA over internal docs).

Quick recap from discovery:
- Volume: ~60k requests/month initially, peak TPS ~1.2
- Latency target: 300–500ms p50 for single-turn summarization
- Quality: high factuality required for compliance responses
- Cost sensitivity: prefer cost-efficient options for scale with an option to upgrade for high-quality flows

Attached is a short PDF with the shortlist and a workbook with benchmark numbers. High-level recommendations below: 

Recommended shortlist (rationale in attached PDF):
1) small-redwood-v2-7B (quantized) — Best cost/latency tradeoff for high throughput; good on summarization with prompt engineering; expected p50 ~180–300ms on our dedicated instances; lowest per-token cost.
2) mid-redwood-13B (int8) — Better quality for edge-case factuality; p50 ~350–500ms; recommended for higher-risk responses and as a fall-back for verification flows.
3) open-claude-equivalent-11B (float16) — Strong instruction-following and safety profile; slightly higher cost but proven in our benchmarks for complex summaries.

Suggested next steps:
- Share the attached prompt set we used in evals (acme-prompt-sets-v1.zip) and the benchmark sheet.
- Quick technical sync with David to confirm inference footprint and integration path (15–30m).
- If procurement needs it, we can share a templated mutual action plan and estimated committed pricing.

Links included: Drive shortlist doc, benchmark sheet, and HubSpot record.

I'll follow up with a proposed calendar for the tech sync — does Friday 2/27 10:30am PT work for you?

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Marissa — helpful summary. A few quick questions from our side: 

1) For the small-redwood-v2-7B quantized option, can you share the expected token-level pricing (hosted vs dedicated)? We need ballpark numbers for procurement.
2) For quality: how big were the prompt sets used in the benchmark? We want to understand coverage of our legal/procurement-specific phrasing.
3) Regarding the mid-redwood-13B fallback flow: can we do a routing policy that only sends 10% of responses to the higher-quality model for verification? How would that affect costs?

Friday 10:30am PT works for a tech sync — please send an invite and any prep materials.

—Tom
Director, Customer Experience | Acme Corp
Tom.Jacobs@acme.com

Great questions — answers inline below and attaching the shortlist workbook with more detail.

1) Pricing (ballpark) — hosted vs dedicated:
- small-redwood-v2-7B (quantized): hosted estimate $0.0008 / input-token; dedicated (reserved) estimate $0.00035 / input-token when committed capacity is selected (assumes monthly commit ~2 GPU-equivalent).
- mid-redwood-13B (int8): hosted estimate $0.002 / input-token; dedicated estimate $0.0009 / input-token.
Notes: these are illustrative — final pricing depends on exact throughput, sequence lengths, and commit level. I'll have RevOps/finance provide a formal quote if you want to proceed.

2) Prompt sets used in benchmark:
- We used a ~120-example prompt set covering typical support summaries, 30 examples with legal language, 20 with multi-document QA, and 10 adversarial factuality checks. The full set is in acme-prompt-sets-v1.zip (attached). If you want, we can expand the legal subset to 50 examples to better validate edge cases.

3) Routing policy for fallback verification:
- Yes — you can do percentage-based routing. If 10% of responses go to mid-redwood-13B for verification, expected blended cost increases approximately 12–18% depending on sequence lengths (we include routing overhead and re-check token counts in the workbook). We can simulate with your average length to give a more precise number.

Tech sync: David / Dev will join to walk through inference footprint and integration. Sending a calendar invite for Fri 2/27 10:30am PT now. Prep: please review the bookmarks in the Drive doc and the prompt set zip.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Tom / Sara — quick tech notes ahead of our sync. A few clarifications so we can make the sync actionable: 

- Inference footprint: small-redwood-v2-7B quantized expects ~6GB GPU memory per replica (on our optimized kernel path). mid-redwood-13B int8 requires ~12–16GB depending on KV cache size for your 2k context tests.
- Latency: the p50 numbers in the workbook assume continuous batching with your TPS profile. If you need strict single-request p50 (no batching), add ~60–110ms to the p50.
- Failure/fallback behavior: we recommend an automated A/B rollout for the routing policy (start with 1% mid-13B verification, ramp to 10% after 24–48h if no quality regressions). Our console will surface per-prompt regression alerts tied to your prompt set.
- Eval caveats: the benchmark used synthetic doc fragments representative of your dataset, but not the full proprietary corpus. To address regression risk we suggest: (a) expand the legal prompt subset to 50 examples, (b) run a 48h pilot with production traffic mirrored to a private deployment, and (c) enable the regressions webhook so issues trigger a ticket in your tracker.

I'll walk through the benchmark sheet in the call and run a quick cost simulation based on your average sequence lengths. If you want the pilot, I can prepare the mirror config and the MOP (minimum operational plan) doc after the sync.

Looking forward to the call — invite received and accepted.

-David
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
